chapter: Reel 2: Los Angeles musicians, the Apex and Cotton Club
title: Fess White and Montudie Garland, players who could not read
summary: Howard says tuba player Fess White had his own band but could not read a lick, and bassist Montudie Garland also could not read.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Reading music versus faking and playing by ear

blocks.x: What about -- there was a guy, a tuba player, who would that be, some years ago.
Some years ago?
Yeah, a tuba player from Local 767. Anybody you know play tuba? Fess White, was he a tuba player?
Fess White? He couldn't read.
Yeah, but wasn't he a tuba player?
Yeah, but he couldn't read a lick.
He couldn't, eh? Well, did he work with any bands or anything?
Huh?
Did he work with any bands?
Yeah, he had a band.
Had his own band.
Yeah. Couldn't read a lick. Fess White.
Fess White.
Yeah.
What about Montoull? [Montudi (Garland)] Who was that, a bass player, probably a very active man with many bands.
Montoull, [sic] he could read, but he could play.
He could play but he couldn't read or he could read?
He couldn't.
But he had a good musical background.
He had a good -- yeah, but he hasn't learned to read today yet. Today, yet, I mean, today.
